analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md is visible: base lines 1381-1756 (historical release notes) and head lines 1-232 (new entries). No source code or tests were supplied, so every behavioral claim is unverified. Security-relevant claims in the head entries:
- Autopilot daily earnings floor (head lines 3-8): new financial path touching A-009, TB-006 and TB-008. This is the finding above.
- Machine-scoped Autopilot (lines 14-19): admin-editable per-machine mode. Live control still requires verified identity and consent, and demotion and revocation semantics are described.
- Soft-delete mutation gate (line 82): defaults to false, blocking new erasure confirmations and provider removal. This is a T-059 availability and compliance trade-off, documented as intentional.
- Account erasure fencing (lines 88-106): relates to T-059.
- Provider-bound top-level user, metadata, safety_identifier and prompt_cache_key stripping (line 230): consistent with the caller-field minimization note, and prompt content is not anonymized.
- Cache-attempt bookkeeping bounds (line 231), prefix-cache SSD write budget (line 47) and the SSD env forwarding relate to T-041. No new TTL or at-rest exposure is claimed.
- No PII in coordinator logs (line 114).
- New archive and analytics reader and snapshot mode (lines 154-162).
Next passes should check whether code changes in the same PR implement the floor-baseline exclusions, admin authorization, idempotent settlement and erasure interactions. Nothing in the diff weakens existing documented mitigations.

findings.detail: The changelog describes a new payment feature: a separately funded daily floor of 110% of a frozen 7-day baseline. The baseline includes sponsored inference. New admin endpoints set an absolute pool cap, fund the pool and repair baselines, and an admin-evidenced backfill sets historical opt-in dates. This touches the payment ledger (A-009), TB-006 (admin API), TB-008 (payments) and ADV-001. The canonical model has no threat entry for this path. A malicious provider could inflate its pre-opt-in baseline with sponsored or self-routed inference, or get a payout from baseline-backfill or consent-evidence mistakes, at the cost of the shared pool. Admin-key compromise (T-024) can also now move money through pool funding and baseline repair. The changelog states mitigations (a pool cap, no partial payments, a `history_conflict` hold, and payments defaulting off). They are not mapped to a threat or mitigation, and no source was supplied to verify them. Fix: add threats and mitigations for floor-baseline gaming, admin funding and backfill abuse, and duplicate or alias machine receipts, and confirm in code that the 7-day baseline excludes self-dealing or sponsored traffic.
findings.title: New Autopilot earnings-floor payout path (admin funding, baseline backfill) has no threat-model coverage
